subject: ADD statement
notes: READ: the grammar alternative `ADD (CORRESPONDING | CORR) dataReference TO receivingIdentifier roundedPhrase? conditionalPhrases END_ADD?` (addStatement's first alternative, CobolParserCore.g4) and CorrespondingBinder.BindAddCorresponding, `add.CORRESPONDING() is not null || add.CORR() is not null ? Bind(CorrVerb.Add, add.dataReference(), add.receivingIdentifier(), ...) : BoundRejected.Report(... StatementFormatShape ...)`. The two spellings are ONE grammar alternative and ONE boolean disjunction feeding ONE Bind call, so there is no second dispatch arm that could carry different behaviour -- the equivalence is structural rather than a pair of parallel code paths (the two-arm-dispatch failure shape does not apply here). Neither token is edition-gated: no ConstructRegistry row in tests/version-matrix/constructs.json mentions CORR or CORRESPONDING, and Annex E carries no ADD entry, so the batch default editions stand. TEST HONESTY: the golden cited exercises the CORRESPONDING spelling on ADD; the CORR spelling is exercised on SUBTRACT (conformance-test:CorrespondingDifferentialTests.SubtractCorr_TargetMinusSource_CorrToken), through subtractStatement's sibling alternative (CobolParserCore.g4) and the identical `sub.CORRESPONDING() is not null || sub.CORR() is not null` disjunction -- so the CORR-on-ADD spelling specifically has no test of its own. Adding `ADD CORR SRC TO DST` to an existing CORR golden would make the coverage exhaustive; nothing about the code makes it a risk. || UPHELD, with evidence the record did not have. The structural argument is only sound if the two spellings are also indistinguishable to the LEXER, which I checked rather than assumed: Core/CobolLexer.g4:455 `CORR : 'CORR' ;` and :459 `CORRESPONDING : 'CORRESPONDING' ;` are both UNCONDITIONAL token rules -- no `{isXXXX()}?` version predicate on either -- and ANTLR's maximal-munch keeps CORRESPONDING whole rather than splitting it into CORR + a word, so neither spelling can degrade into a data-name at any edition. Had CORR been edition-gated or context-sensitive, `ADD CORR X TO Y` would have fallen to grammar alternative 2 and bound CORR as an ADDEND -- a silent wrong answer -- which is the failure mode this check rules out. Also verified: alternative 1 precedes alternative 2, so the Format-3 parse always wins, and BindAddCorresponding's `else` arm is unreachable (BindAdd routes here only when `sendingOperand()` is empty, which only alternative 1 produces). I also independently confirmed the edition claim per ground rule 4: Annex E (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:42847 onward) lists no ADD substantive change, and the rule text carries no edition qualifier, so the batch default 85,2002,2014,2023 is the derived answer, not a copied one. CONFORMS-but-thinly-tested is the correct outcome here (ground rule 3), and the record's own honesty note about the CORR-on-ADD spelling stands.
